{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABdS3eFw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhGzpDk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 247, "title": "Implement opt-in in-page voice typing using an assigned Graph Library graph", "body": "## Goal

Implement browser-page **voice typing from a small microphone icon next to the focused editable field**, driven by a Graph Library graph, **only when explicitly enabled by the user**.

This is an opt-in capability, **not** a permanent global mic overlay for everyone who uses other graph features. Preserve the existing Live transcription / model management UX for users who never enable Web voice typing.

## Owner clarification: completion scope

This clarification supersedes earlier Issue text and comments that made manual Chrome checks required post-merge verification. Complete this Issue through implementation, relevant available automated tests, normal review and merge. Manual installed-Chrome checks are **later follow-up only**, not acceptance criteria and not blockers for review, merge, Issue closure or the Project Done status. Do not create a separate Issue for them. A normal `Closes #247` reference is appropriate once the implementation passes review; do not remove/re-add it because these later checks are unperformed.

Keep the requested permission, recording lifecycle, field targeting and insertion behavior implemented and covered by feasible automated checks. Fix demonstrated defects before merge and report actual test results honestly. Do not claim unperformed manual or real-model checks passed. Do not request a human test result solely to complete this Task.

## User experience / agreed behavior

**Graph Library → Default execution targets → Web page voice typing**

- Add a persistent, clearly labeled **Web voice typing ON/OFF switch**.
- **Default OFF**, including existing installations and users with an already assigned `webVoice` graph ID. Assignment does **not** imply consent/enablement.
- Keep the existing selector for the **assigned Web voice typing graph**, keyed by stable graph ID (`assignments.webVoice`), separate from the **Live** assignment.
- With the feature OFF: **no mic icons, injected overlay, background recording, or AI model loading** for this feature on normal Web pages. Use nothing beyond what is needed to support the explicit setting / permissions.
- When toggling ON, explain and request any necessary **website access permission explicitly**; do not quietly add broad persistent site access for nonusers. Handle denial, restricted URLs and sites without permission gracefully. Provide a usable explanation and OFF state when activation is not possible.
- Show a brief, actionable message if no Web voice graph is assigned or if the assigned graph is unsuitable. **Never silently substitute the Live default graph.**
- Once enabled and authorized, when a user focuses a supported editable field on a Web page, show a **small floating mic icon visually attached to that field**, ideally at the upper/right edge without changing page layout or covering existing controls.
- Click icon: prepare assigned graph's required models in the extension-owned runtime (show compact **Preparing…** state if needed), then with explicit microphone permission **start dictation into the original field**. Click again: **Stop** gracefully. Distinguish Idle, Preparing, Recording, Stopping, Error states (icon + accessible labels), with an obvious way to stop.
- Do not open a full Live UI popup to start voice input; the page-local experience must remain lightweight. Normal page editing and Send/Submit remain entirely under user control.

Target mental model: **focus input → click mic → speak → text appears there → click to stop**.

## Graph wiring and eligibility

Reuse existing concrete Nodes and graph execution contracts, not a parallel speech-recognition implementation.

An example compatible graph:

```text
MicrophoneAudio.audio → SpeechToTextReazonSpeech.audio
SpeechToTextReazonSpeech.final → FocusedInputTextOutputNode.text
```

- Graph Library should offer/select **only compatible executable graphs** for the Web voice execution target, or display a clear reason that a graph is incompatible and prevent enabling / starting with it.
- Validate **a complete executable path originating at `MicrophoneAudio` and ending at `FocusedInputTextOutputNode`**, carrying typed compatible data via actual graph edges, rather than relying on graph names, tags or presence of Nodes alone. Allow legitimate intermediate compatible processors (text formatter, translation, etc.), preserving the user's graph flexibility; don't hardcode a single ASR model.
- For the initial in-page workflow, exclude/reject graphs requiring **`ChromeTabAudio` or unavailable `SelectedPageMediaAudio` active capture paths**, unless their independent side effects are explicitly handled without hidden tab capture. No implied page/tab capture or unrelated page modifications.
- A graph can have other optional outputs but must not unexpectedly trigger unrelated UI actions/side effects by simply clicking a mic. Clearly document and test what the in-page runtime runs.
- Reuse `GraphLibrary.assignments.webVoice` and a stable graph snapshot at session start. A running session must **not** change graph midway when the Library assignment or graph contents change.
- Keep existing Graph JSON schema/version 15, ports and Node IDs unchanged. Store the enablement preference **separately** from the graph content/assignment, with validated persistence and safe cross-tab sync.

## Content Script / floating control

- Extend the MV3 manifest and Content Script architecture using **least-privilege permissions**. The current manifest has `activeTab`, `tabCapture`, and `scripting` but no global content script; do not assume that `activeTab` alone authorizes background injection into all pages.
- With permission and ON, observe focus on supported writable text controls: at minimum **`textarea` and normal text `input`**; support ordinary `contenteditable` safely where practical. Don't attach to `password`, OTP, payment, hidden/readonly/disabled, noneditable or clearly sensitive inputs, or restricted internal/browser pages. Avoid broad unreviewed content collection.
- Use a small **extension-owned, isolated floating widget** (e.g. shadow-root overlay) positioned from the target's bounding box. Do not permanently change DOM structure inside host controls, break CSS/layout or hijack page clicks/keys. Reposition on scroll, resize, zoom, layout changes; hide/clean up on blur or navigation when idle.
- Preserve the original selection/caret even though the mic icon receives the click; **bind the whole session to that specific field/document**, not whatever element happens to be focused later. Don't redirect to another field after focus changes.
- While recording, keep an unobtrusive accessible way to stop (even if the target loses focus). Show target disconnected/unsupported errors explicitly; stop safely if target is detached, frame navigates, or tab closes.
- Allow one in-page voice-typing session at a time across tabs, with explicit busy indication. Do not terminate a separate running Live session or silently steal its microphone/audio/GPU resources. Prevent conflicting starts safely; treat full concurrent execution as a future task.
- No auto-start on focus, no auto-send/submit, no speech-triggered submit or website navigation. Manual keyboard editing continues to work.

## Extension-owned inference and field insertion

- Refactor/reuse the existing `TabSession`, `buildGraph`, `MicrophoneAudio`, ASR/translators and `FocusedInputTextOutputNode` where feasible. **Content Script is the UI/target bridge, not the model inference host**; no duplicate worker architecture or inference in the page.
- Use an appropriate durable extension-owned document/context for microphone/model work when Live is not open (e.g. evaluate MV3 Offscreen Document). Validate the actual Chrome API capabilities and gesture/permission code paths with available automated installed-extension tests; native permission-prompt checks by the owner are later follow-up, not completion requirements. An MV3 service worker alone is not a substitute for a DOM/WebGPU/microphone environment. Do not claim unsupported Offscreen/WebGPU/gUM behavior; choose a functioning alternative if necessary without bringing back an unwanted Live popup.
- On mic activation, open the selected graph as a **model-prepared** session: verified local cached weights only, compatible with the #239 lifecycle, with visible loading and actionable Models/Graph recovery for missing assets or unsupported GPU. No remote inference or recording-time model download. Initiate microphone access only as an explicit result of mic interaction; handle user activation/async readiness and permission denials correctly.
- Deliver output only to the **selected, authorized page document and editor element**. The current `extension/page-target.js` / `extension/page-output-node.js` presume toolbar-invoked `activeTab` and a focused field; adapt their secure addressing/handshake to the **page mic gesture** without granting an unrelated target. Enforce tab/frame/document/field identity and per-session capability; reject stale or spoofed/misrouted messages.
- Insert **committed/final TEXT** exactly once at the saved selection/caret (or well-defined insertion point). Avoid duplicate/replayed provisional results; optionally show interim recognition **as a noncommitted preview** associated with the field, not repeatedly appended to its value. Update ordinary input controls through appropriate native editing/input events so controlled forms and undo/editing work as well as possible. Do not overwrite the whole field, silently submit or reinsert on ambiguous timeout.
- Document supported field types and known limitations with rich editors, Shadow DOM, cross-origin iframes and websites with custom event handlers. Do not claim universal input compatibility without real tests.
- Stop should drain accepted final output before release; Cancel/permission revoke/field removal/tab close should abort and suppress late replies; leave unrelated page text intact. Keep temporary captured audio and transcript strictly local, without unsolicited persistence.

## Failure and lifecycle behavior

- OFF immediately removes injected controls and stops any ongoing in-page voice session safely; explicit disabling should revoke/stop the session rather than leave a live mic.
- Graph assignment changes, graph edits, page refreshes, tab close, extension restart, permission revoke, model failure, and GPU loss must not leave a recording running, wrong-field insertion, orphaned overlays, stale `Ready`/recording indicators, or hanging Workers. Future sessions use the new assignment after the active session ends.
- Explicit errors (no compatible assigned graph, missing mic permission, missing model cache, unsupported site/frame/input, busy session) should be visible near the icon or in Graph Library and actionable; do not hide a nonfunctional button or silently act on a different graph.
- Protect against unintended elevation of permissions: only install/activate site scripts after feature enablement + user-granted host permission, constrain message senders, and avoid logging/transmitting input field content unnecessarily.

## Implementation touch points

Likely:
- `extension/graph-library.html`, `extension/graph-library-page.js`, `extension/graph-library.js`: explicit preference and graph selection/compatibility reporting; remove “not yet available” copy once working.
- `extension/manifest.json`, `extension/background.js`: explicit site permission and Content Script / extension-host lifecycle.
- New focused-field mic overlay Content Script and its CSS/communication layer.
- `extension/page-target.js`, `extension/page-agent.js`, `extension/page-output-node.js`: secure target identity, selection and insertion.
- `extension/session.js`, `extension/graph-runtime.js`, `extension/media-source.js`: reuse prepared runtime and microphone session without a Live popup.
- Browser/MV3 E2E tests, docs and manual permission guidance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After install/upgrade, **Web voice typing is OFF by default**, including when a Web graph was previously assigned. No mic controls injected for an OFF user.
- [ ] User can explicitly turn Web voice typing ON/OFF in Graph Library and select a compatible saved graph; the setting and assignment persist independently and survive page/reload synchronization.
- [ ] Incompatible graphs are identified using actual executable `MicrophoneAudio → … → FocusedInputTextOutputNode` connectivity, with actionable explanation; the Live assignment remains independent.
- [ ] With permission/ON, mic icon appears beside eligible editable inputs but not password/disabled/readonly/sensitive fields, restricted pages, or unsupported contexts; no host-page layout breakage.
- [ ] Clicking the mic triggers preparation (if not already ready), explicit mic permission, graph execution, the implemented microphone → ASR → originally chosen field insertion path, and repeat-click Stop. No full Live UI needed.
- [ ] First/final utterance inserted **exactly once** at the proper caret, with no provisional duplication, unintended focus shift, wrong-field write or auto-submit. Editing after insertion continues to work.
- [ ] No model inference in Content Script; same saved graph semantics/workers/verified assets as existing runtime. Missing cache/hardware produces error rather than network inference or silently using a different graph.
- [ ] Single-session and target identity enforcement across multiple tabs; changing focus, active tab, saved graph or navigating does not change the output target of a running session.
- [ ] ON→OFF, Stop/Cancel, navigation, worker/model error, permission loss and extension close clean up audio, Workers, GPU and overlays without late writes.
- [ ] Relevant deterministic tests for preference/eligibility, permission and session messages, cleanup and field insertion, plus available automated packaged-Chrome-extension tests using controlled input/inference where appropriate. Cover native input + textarea, field/caret behavior, no-auto-send, stop, multi-tab and disabled state. Clearly report actual passes/failures and distinguish controlled/mocked coverage from real microphone/model coverage. Human-operated permission dialogs and real microphone checks listed below are not required to satisfy this criterion.

## Later owner checks (not completion criteria)

These are notes for later, not required post-merge verification. Their unperformed status must not keep this Issue open, block merge, or prevent the Task/Project item becoming complete. Do not turn these notes into another Issue or a new checklist gate.

- In installed Chrome, manually try native website/microphone permission denial and grant, then real microphone dictation into input and textarea. Check caret placement, single insertion, Stop and no automatic submission, and record Chrome version and observed results when performed.
- During recording, revoke microphone permission in Chrome settings and later check capture/session shutdown, the actionable error and suppression of late insertion. Record the actual result when performed.

## Non-goals / keep lean

Do not add site-by-site rules, unrelated per-graph display tags, an always-visible global overlay, multi-user/shared sessions, new ASR models, new pipeline port/schema types or unrestricted parallel graph sessions in this Issue. Maintain the current Graph Library layout and the minimalist Live UI.
